question_text: A 82-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her son because he is concerned about her forgetfulness for the past 2 years. She occasionally walks into a room and forgets why she went there and often forgets where she left her keys. She is sometimes unable to recall a familiar individual's name. She reports that she has become slower at completing sudoku puzzles. She has been living independently since the death of her husband 3 years ago. She goes shopping, cooks her own meals, and plays bridge with her friends every weekend. She is not anxious about her memory lapses. She has no trouble sleeping but has been getting up earlier than she used to. She has hypertension that is managed with hydrochlorothiazide. She appears healthy. Vital signs are within normal limits. She is oriented to person, place, and time. Examination shows a normal gait. She describes her mood as “good” and her speech is normal. Her thought process is organized and her judgement is intact. She makes one error when performing serial sevens. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
